stemBlocks.value: Think first: Divide through by 2 first so the x² term stands alone — completing the square is much cleaner that way.

solutionSteps.instruction: Combine the constants and isolate the square.
Take the square root of both sides, keeping both signs.

strategyBlocks.value: Divide the whole equation by 2, complete the square, isolate it, then square-root both sides with a ±.

whyThisWorks.value: The method only produces a perfect square when the x² coefficient is 1, so dividing through by 2 is the enabling first move; dividing an equation by a non-zero number does not change its roots. After that the equation reduces to (x − 3)² = 5.5, which two values of x satisfy — one above 3 and one an equal distance below it. That symmetry about x = 3 is the axis of symmetry of the parabola.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing only the x-terms by 2 and leaving the 7 untouched.
